items.method: Cross-read the dealer-positioning corridor (regime sign, flip, put and call walls, front expected move, signed net GEX and the gamma playbook) against the benchmark's carried price relative to that corridor, then layer the confirming internals (cash-market breadth versus the 60% participation line, single-name call-versus-put premium and the calm conditional-volatility regime) and finally test them against the intraday auction state and control, judging whether a calm positive-gamma pin sitting on the flip is genuinely damping or is masking a reversal-prone auction, and anchoring a direction-correct invalidation below the benchmark at the put-wall loss that would flip dealers back to amplifying a downside break.
items.note: The genuinely new configuration this window is that the dealer structure has flipped from the amplifying negative-gamma stance of the prior window into a damping positive-gamma pin, and it lands exactly where the benchmark is trading. SPY dealers now read positive gamma with signed net GEX about +5.49M, the flip at 768.22, the put wall 765 and the call wall 770 inside a tight plus-or-minus 3.98 front expected move on a 0.1401 ATM IV, and the gamma playbook is pin-to-maxpain with patient conviction and a same-session-fade hold. The benchmark is carried at 768.76, essentially on the 768.22 flip and hemmed inside the 765/770 wall corridor. Supporting internals lean the same constructive way: market-heatmap breadth is broad at 67% of 134 constituents against a 60% threshold, single-name option premium is call-heavy at a 0.6973 call fraction ($876.3M calls against $380.3M puts across 12 tickers, with the heaviest print a TSLA 375 call at $40.9M on 5.6x open interest one day out), and the volatility model reads a calm 10.267% regime. The dissonance is that the most recent intraday auction is a Reversal risk session under Algo-controlled control at VWAP 768.96 rather than the trend-up auction the constructive internals would imply, so the calm mechanical pin is being priced over a two-sided, reversal-prone tape. The confirming trigger for the constructive-pin case is the benchmark holding above the 768.22 flip and grinding toward the 770 call wall while breadth stays above 60%; the constructive-pin lean is invalidated on a daily close below ~765.00 on SPY, which loses the 765 put wall, drops spot beneath the flip into negative-gamma territory where dealer hedging would sell weakness, and would confirm the reversal-risk auction over the pin.
items.title: A positive-gamma pin sits directly on top of a reversal-risk tape: SPY dealers flipped to positive gamma with the flip at 768.22 and walls 765/770 inside a plus-or-minus 3.98 expected move while the benchmark is carried at 768.76 right on the flip, breadth is broad at 67% of 134 constituents and single-name premium is call-heavy at a 0.6973 call fraction — yet the most recent intraday auction reads Reversal risk under Algo-controlled control at VWAP 768.96, so the mechanical pin and the auction character disagree

items.method: Cross-read the firming US internals (broad breadth above the participation line, call-heavy single-name premium, a calm volatility regime) against where leadership is actually being scored — the global-rotation composite ranking country ETFs versus ACWI and the real-assets 0-100 composite ranking crypto, broad-commodity, bitcoin, agriculture, oil, gold and silver vehicles — to test whether risk appetite still concentrates offshore and in real assets while the domestic tape merely confirms, then, finding the leadership cluster resolves only to relative-strength scores and composite rankings rather than any price level on a committed-universe instrument, withhold the tactical call rather than publish one that resolves to unscoreable.
items.note: The second cross-model pattern this window is that the leadership scores continue to point offshore and into real assets even as the domestic tape stays firm, so the migration remains a where-is-the-bid observation rather than a confirmation of index direction. The US picture is constructive: market-heatmap breadth is broad at 67% of 134 constituents, single-name option premium is call-heavy at a 0.6973 call fraction, and the benchmark is carried at 768.76 in a calm VIX 14.95 regime. Against that, global rotation ranks EWS (Singapore) first at 93.9/100 versus the US-heavy ACWI, with EWC (Canada) 74.4, EWT (Taiwan) 74, EWJ (Japan) 71.4 and EWZ (Brazil) 70.7 ahead of a middling US read. Real assets are led by crypto and broad commodities — ETH-USD 77.1, DBC 74.6 (six-month momentum +20.72%), PDBC 74.5 (+20.92%), bitcoin IBIT 71.8 and BTC-USD 68.9, agriculture DBA 71.3 — while oil (USO) 67.2 is a firmer uptrend (+48.49% six-month) and gold (GLD) 40.8 is mixed and rate-shadowed with a -11.93% six-month pulse, silver (SLV) 18.1 weaker still at -19.05% six-month. Sector rotation echoes the risk tone domestically, rotating toward XLC as XLE rolls over. The pattern is coherent but it resolves entirely to relative-strength composite scores and country and vehicle rankings, none of which is a price level on a committed-universe instrument, so there is no direction-correct level at which the migration would be proven wrong. Rather than publish a tactical rotation call that could never be scored, the call is withheld; the observation stands as context that the marginal bid is concentrating offshore and in crypto and broad commodities while precious metals lag.
items.title: Leadership keeps being scored offshore and in real assets while US internals stay constructive: global rotation ranks EWS (Singapore) far ahead of the US-heavy ACWI and the real-assets composite leads with crypto and broad commodities, gold weak and silver weaker — a where-is-the-bid migration that resolves only to relative-strength scores, so no scoreable tactical call is published
